verdict.rationale: Teams messaging/collaboration rides on Microsoft Graph, which exposes a machine-readable OData CSDL metadata document ($metadata) confirmed live via hands-on probe (HTTP 200), functioning as an OpenAPI-equivalent spec; Graph also has documented OpenAPI descriptions elsewhere in Microsoft's ecosystem. However, Teams-specific developer docs (learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/platform) do not surface a dedicated OpenAPI/Swagger file, and probes for llms.txt, docs-md, and openapi.json at the Teams docs root all returned 404. missing for 10: a Teams-specific (not just general Graph) downloadable OpenAPI file, first-party documentation explicitly advertising an OpenAPI spec for Teams APIs, and independent confirmation beyond the raw $metadata probe.
